text:
Bitcoin continues its tight consolidation near $64,000 as broader sentiment remains risk-averse, with the Crypto Fear & Greed Index lingering at 25. Regional liquidity is contracting, with South Korean trading volumes hitting two-year lows amidst equity volatility. Simultaneously, the regulatory landscape is shifting toward structural policymaking. The SEC has formalized three proposals targeting broker-dealer custody, while the expiration of the European Union's MiCA transitional window forces the market into a harmonized compliance era.

Macroeconomic uncertainty remains the primary headwind for digital asset expansion. With the Federal Reserve holding the target funds rate at 3.50%–3.75%, markets are heavily weighting the upcoming July 28 FOMC meeting. New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's pivot toward strict data dependency has injected opacity into the rate path. This elevated rate environment and persistent policy ambiguity continue to mechanically constrain non-yielding assets, tethering Bitcoin to the broader fate of global liquidity.
